clue.text: Society girl cutting modern Hungarian city

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a young woman introduced into high society

indicators.note: cutting here means trimming the final letter off the next word

parts.note: modern means recent

explanation.surface: A debutante seems to be slicing through some up-to-date Hungarian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' looks like the girl's action on the city, but it trims RECENT to RECEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Debrecen is the second-largest city in Hungary, in the east of the country.

clue.text: Top dog and poor stray on the Fife coast

indicators.note: top means the first letter of the word that follows
poor signals the next word's letters are put in bad order

explanation.surface: A top dog and a poor stray animal wandering the Fife coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: Dysart is a former burgh on the Firth of Forth, now part of Kirkcaldy in Fife, Scotland.

clue.text: Costermonger's cart in oven, reportedly in Cumbrian town

parts.note: a costermonger is a London street seller of fruit, who sells from a barrow
taken as written

indicators.note: reportedly means the oven word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a furnace is an industrial oven

explanation.surface: A street trader's barrow ends up in an oven somewhere in Cumbria.
explanation.walkthrough: A costermonger is a traditional London street seller of fruit and veg.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrow-in-Furness is an industrial and shipbuilding town on the Cumbrian coast of north-west England.

clue.text: Grebes swimming round edge of jetty in Danish port

indicators.note: round means the jumbled birds' letters go about the edge letter
swimming means the birds' letters move about freely
edge of means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Water birds swim around the end of a jetty in a Danish harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges GREBES to ESBERG, and 'round' wraps that around J.
explanation.definitionFit: Esbjerg is a seaport on the west coast of Jutland in Denmark.

clue.text: Cathedral city with some chapel. Yes!

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow is used

explanation.surface: A cathedral city has its share of chapels, emphatically so.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely in Cambridgeshire is a small English city famous for its cathedral.

clue.text: Sketch heart-transplant in Australian city

indicators.note: the heart of the word for sketch, its middle pair, is transplanted so the two central letters swap places

parts.note: to sketch is to draw
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drawing of a heart-transplant operation done somewhere in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart-transplant' swaps the middle letters of DRAW to give DARW.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwin is the capital of Australia's Northern Territory.

clue.text: This Californian city with courts would be South American

indicators.note: would be says the city's letters together with the courts' letters could be rearranged into the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A Californian city given some courts would supposedly turn South American.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: the answer plus COURTS makes an anagram of SOUTH AMERICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaheim is a city in Orange County, southern California, home of Disneyland.

clue.text: This could be 20's warmest northern resort!

indicators.note: could be means the letters given may be rearranged into something else

parts.note: 20 is the answer to 20-across, the continent, and the 's adds an S
taken as written

explanation.surface: This could be the warmest northern holiday spot in Europe!
explanation.walkthrough: The S of '20's' is part of the anagram fodder, with EUROPE from 20-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Weston-super-Mare is a seaside holiday town on the Somerset coast of England.

clue.text: It's strange to keep navy where Yale is situated

parts.note: something strange is new or unfamiliar
to keep is to have

explanation.surface: It seems odd that a famous university should maintain a navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale University is located in New Haven, Connecticut.

clue.text: Almost certain a laurel-tree's on old film in Indonesian city

indicators.note: almost means the word is taken short of its last letter

parts.note: certain means sure
the bay is the laurel tree
A was an old British film certificate classification

explanation.surface: A laurel almost surely features in some old film set in Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: A was the old British certificate for films that children could see only with an adult.
explanation.definitionFit: Surabaya is a large port city on the Indonesian island of Java.

clue.text: Hostilities observed in capital in 20

parts.note: hostilities between nations make a war
observed means saw

explanation.surface: Fighting witnessed in a European capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is the answer to 20-across, the continent, so the definition is a European capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland, a country on the European continent.

clue.text: Rough scene he'd entered in Dutch city

indicators.note: entered means he'd goes into the jumbled scene letters
rough means the letters of the scene are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowdy scene he walked into in a Dutch city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' rearranges SCENE to ENSCE, and 'entered' puts HED inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Enschede is a city in the eastern Netherlands, close to the German border.

clue.text: Bay horse spoken of on river

indicators.note: spoken of means we take how the horse word sounds, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed coat; a bay roan has a reddish-brown base

explanation.surface: A brown horse is talked about on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a major European waterway flowing from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Nominates new state

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters before it

explanation.surface: Someone puts forward a newly formed state or government.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty United States, in the Upper Midwest.

clue.text: Whisky glen — enigma or puzzle?

indicators.note: puzzle means the preceding letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Is this whisky's name an enigma or a puzzle?
explanation.walkthrough: The answer follows 'glen' to name the whisky: Glenmorangie.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenmorangie is a Highland single malt Scotch, so this is the part after Glen.

clue.text: Large room for car missing rear half in Scottish town

parts.note: large means big

indicators.note: missing rear half means the back three of the six letters are dropped

parts.note: a garage is a room for a car

explanation.surface: A big garage for a vehicle that is short of its back end, in a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Biggar is a small market town in South Lanarkshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Timeless holiday tented area in fells in Stirlingshire

indicators.note: timeless means T, the abbreviation for time, is removed

parts.note: a holiday area full of tents is a campsite

explanation.surface: An eternal holiday campsite set among hills in Stirlingshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Campsie Fells are a range of hills north of Glasgow, partly in the old county of Stirlingshire.

clue.text: Top-class grub served on Thursday in Liverpudlian suburb

parts.note: A1, written AI in crosswords, means first-rate

indicators.note: served means the food word is dished up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: First-rate food dished up on a Thursday in a Liverpool suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: Aigburth is a residential district in south Liverpool, by the Mersey.

clue.text: Remains at village near Whitchurch in Shropshire

definitions.meaning: what is left after burning, cinders and powder
a small village in north Shropshire, England, close to the market town of Whitchurch

explanation.surface: Something remains in a Shropshire village near Whitchurch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the powdery residue of fire, and also a village name in Shropshire.

clue.text: Iranian city is cooler, with hot area inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: inside means the hot and area letters go within the cooler

parts.note: a fan is a device that cools
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An Iranian city is cooler, though there is a hot area within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Isfahan is a historic city in central Iran, famous for its mosques and bridges.

clue.text: Chap's on steep rock-face at Wirral town

parts.note: chap is a man, he; with 's for is
a steep face of rock is a wall

explanation.surface: A man is clinging to a cliff in a town on the Wirral.
explanation.definitionFit: Heswall is a town on the Wirral peninsula in Merseyside, overlooking the Dee estuary.

clue.text: Outpour during the middle of the week on the continent

indicators.note: during means the middle letters go around, the poured-out letters sitting in their span
the middle of a word means its central letters

parts.note: read as out plus pour: pour with its letters put out of order

explanation.surface: A downpour falls midweek across the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outpour' must be split: 'Out' is the anagram signal working on 'pour', a trick the single printed word hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is one of the world's continents.

clue.text: Polish religious statue on river crossed by Caesar

parts.note: to polish is to rub
an icon is a religious image

explanation.surface: Someone buffs up a sacred figure beside the river Caesar crossed.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar crossed the Rubicon in 49 BC, starting civil war with Rome.

clue.text: US state where leading artist turns up for another

indicators.note: leading means the removed letters are at the very front of the other state

parts.note: another US state, one of the fifty

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A US state where a top painter appears in place of someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a state; put RA turned round in front of it and you get another state, Arkansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is a Midwestern state of the USA.

clue.text: Idiots further up reportedly in county

parts.note: berk is British slang for an idiot

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for further up is taken by its sound

parts.note: further up means higher

explanation.surface: Fools climbing higher, it is said, in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'higher' and 'hire' sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Berkshire is an English shire in the south of the country, west of London.

clue.text: Polish revolutionary's mother country?

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the polish word is read backwards

parts.note: to polish is to rub
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Is a Polish revolutionary's mother country Poland?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital pretends to be about Poland; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma, now officially Myanmar, is a nation in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Small railway on online auction site on the Sussex coast

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway
eBay is the well-known online auction site

explanation.surface: A miniature railway put up for sale on eBay, somewhere on the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye Bay is an inlet of the English Channel by the town of Rye in East Sussex.

clue.text: Money for cleaners at Scottish RAF base

parts.note: the leu is the currency of Romania
a char, or charwoman, is a British word for a domestic cleaner

explanation.surface: Cash paid to the cleaning staff at an air force station in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: RAF Leuchars is a military airfield in Fife, Scotland, near St Andrews.

clue.text: Loch near Fort William showing in Sheila's mirror

indicators.note: showing in means the letters can be seen inside the name that follows

explanation.surface: A Scottish loch is seen reflected in a woman's mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch Eil is a sea loch in the Highlands of Scotland, west of Fort William.

clue.text: Topless game with the French at town near Hull

indicators.note: topless means the board game's first letter is removed

parts.note: chess is a board game
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A game of strip chess with French players near Hull.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessle is a town on the Humber estuary just west of Kingston upon Hull in Yorkshire.

clue.text: Whence a mare for Swann's partner in Belgium

definitions.meaning: Henry VIII called Anne of Cleves his 'mare' from this region
Michael, the singing partner of Donald Swann in the comic duo
a historic region of northern Belgium

explanation.surface: Where a horse came from for Swann's companion in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII reputedly called his fourth wife, Anne of Cleves, a mare from Flanders; Flanders and Swann were a British comic-song duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanders is the Dutch-speaking northern region of Belgium, a surname, and Anne of Cleves's nickname source.
